newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan dollar deposits at banks continuing - sources.
newsitem.headline: Japan dollar deposits at banks continuing - sources.

text.p: Japanese monetary authorities appear to be continuing discreet deposits of dollars at Japanese banks facing difficulties raising funds in overseas money markets, banking sources said on Monday.

"(The authorities) are continuing to provide funds so banks will not face liquidity problems towards the end of the year," one banking source said. Worries about the health of Japanese banks have increased since the collapse of Hanwa Bank Ltd in November, increasing the cost to them of raising funds overseas.
Last year, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) boosted the volume of its dollar deposits at commercial banks, using cash raised through dollar-buying intervention.

Bankers said the MOF had continued to park substantial amounts of dollars in private banks. Analysts said the fund movements were effectively subsidies as the authorities were lending to private banks at lower rates than their actual fund-raising costs.
The MOF and Bank of Japan customarily do not disclose details of their management of external reserves.
